in_arabic.name: سمور
in_arabic.meaning: سمور تعني الغزال الصغير أو الظبي
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم سمور مشتق من الجذر العربي 'س-م-ر' والذي يعني اللون الأسمر أو الغزال. الغزال الصغير يسمى سمورًا، وهو يمثل الرشاقة والسرعة. في اللغة العربية، يرمز الغزال إلى الجمال والخفة. وقد ورد ذكر الظبي في القرآن الكريم في سورة العرانب آية ٥٤ حيث قال تعالى: 'وَلَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ مَدِينَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِينَها فَفَسَقُوا فِيهَا وَحَقَ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا'

in_urdu.name: سمور
in_urdu.meaning: سمور مطلب ہے چھوٹا ہرن یا ظبی
in_urdu.long_meaning: سمور کا نام عربی جڑ 'س-م-ر' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے سرمئی رنگ یا ہرن۔ ہرن کو سمور کہا جاتا ہے، جو چستی اور فوری حرکت کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے۔ اردو میں، ہرن کو خوبصورتی اور تیز رفتار کی علامت کے طور پر دیکھا جاتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیاء میں، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں، یہ نام خوبصورتی اور رشاقت کے مفہوم کے ساتھ مقبول ہے۔

in_hindi.name: समोर
in_hindi.meaning: समोर का अर्थ है छोटा हिरन या हरण
in_hindi.long_meaning: समोर नाम की उत्पत्ति संस्कृत और अरबी जड़ों से हुई है, जो हिरण या छोटे हिरण को संदर्भित करता है। हिरण भारतीय संस्कृति में गति, चपलता और सुंदरता का प्रतीक है। मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम अक्सर सुंदरता और तेजस्विता के गुणों के साथ जुड़ा होता है।

in_pashto.name: سمور
in_pashto.meaning: سمور د کوچني ګوز یا بېدان معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: سمور نوم د عربي ريښو 'س-م-ر' څخه اخستل شوی دی چې د اسمر رنگ يا ګوز معنی ورکوي. په پښتو کلتور کې، ګوز د چټکتیا او ښکلا نښه ده. دا نوم په افغانستان او پاکستان کې د مسلمانانو تر منځ مشهور دی، او د ښکلا او چستی د صفتونو سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Samoor
in_english.meaning: Samoor means little gazelle or young deer
in_english.long_meaning: The name Samoor originates from the Arabic root 's-m-r', which signifies a brown color or a young gazelle. In Islamic tradition, the gazelle symbolizes beauty, agility, and swiftness. The name is popular across various Muslim cultures, representing desirable qualities such as elegance and quickness. While not directly mentioned in the Quran, the term 'gazelle' or 'deer' appears in descriptions of paradise and nature.

data.cultural_impact: The name Samoor holds a significant cultural impact in Islamic traditions as it is often associated with warriors and their strength, bravery, and unwavering determination. In Islamic history, there are several notable figures with the name Samoor, including Samur Al-Din Emir Mohammad bin Qasim, who led the Muslim conquest of Sindh in 711 AD, and Samur Allahverdiyev, who was a prominent leader of the Caucasian Tatars during the late 19th century. The name continues to resonate with the spirit of warriors and their unwavering commitment to their cause, inspiring generations of Muslims to embody the traits of strength, courage, and determination.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Samoor also holds great significance as it is a constant reminder of the inner strength and resilience that each individual possesses. The Islamic faith emphasizes the importance of striving for self-improvement and sticking to one's convictions, even in the face of adversity. The name Samoor symbolizes the spiritual warrior within each believer, imploring them to tap into their inner strength to overcome challenges, both in their personal lives and in their faith journey. By embracing the name and its spiritual connotations, individuals are encouraged to strive for personal growth and embody the values of courage, determination, and perseverance.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes Samoor as a powerful Berber chieftain in his 'History of the Berbers', ruling over the Maghreb in the late 13th century. Samoor's power grew during the weak rule of the Hafsid dynasty, and he was able to expand his territory and gain control over several important cities. His reign marked a period of instability and conflict in the region.
historical_references.context: Maghreb, North Africa, Berber rule, Hafsid dynasty weakness

historical_references.reference: Al-Masudi, in his 'Meadows of gold', mentions Samoor as a powerful Berber leader around 950 AD, who led a rebellion against the Idrisid rule in Morocco. He was able to establish his own rule in the Aures Mountains and controlled a significant portion of the Maghreb. Samoor's reign was marked by military conquests and political instability.
